title: Require Categorical Service Context Boundaries
forbids: a root base without the deps, scope, config, invocation, and provided lanes; root middleware not authored from base.middleware; a noncanonical module middleware leaf or one authored from neither base.middleware nor the exact lower-camel impl.<module>.middleware branch; a middleware index without only documented semantic aliases to simple leaves; module.ts bypassing that middleware index; explicit .use type arguments; a module without inferred inline terminal curation or one that renames context/next, passes or spreads context, projects whole raw lanes through dot or bracket access, or emits a raw-lane output key; or an operation leaf that reopens a raw context lane through property, bracket, or destructuring access
why: One native context author establishes explicit ownership and lifetime lanes. Named middleware enriches that context, while terminal module curation leaves handlers with only their operation vocabulary.
remediate: Declare all five lanes and base = os.$context<Context>() in base.ts. Export documented root context middleware only from base.middleware(...). Give every module middleware leaf a simple kebab-case filename and export one documented context middleware from base.middleware(...) or contract-aware policy from its exact impl.<lowerCamelModule>.middleware(...) branch. Keep middleware/index.ts to documented semantic re-exports from those leaves, and import middleware into module.ts only through ./middleware. Attach each named value once through service.<module>.use(...); use a direct inline service.<module>.use(callback) only when policy requires root-configured output. End module.ts with an inferred inline curation whose context/next names stay stable and whose output selects explicit members without passing, spreading, renaming, or emitting whole raw lanes.
message: Service context must descend through the native five-lane capability funnel.
